LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe storm surge and landslides have disrupted the Central Basin AO. Key bridges are degraded, and debris clearance is ongoing. Three logistics hubs—Supply Depot Alpha (north airhead), Supply Depot Bravo (western railhead), and Supply Depot Charlie (port staging)—hold potable water, food, and medical items for forward distribution across a 3-day window. Five receiving elements—1st Relief Battalion (Central District), 2nd Relief Battalion (Coastal District), 3rd Relief Battalion (Highlands), Field Hospital Sierra, and Shelter Complex Delta—require sustained resupply. Routes include the valley corridor (exposed to rockfall and sporadic security incidents), the coastal roadway (flooded segments), and the highland pass (steep grades, limited convoy speed). Engineering and security teams can clear and escort selected corridors daily but capacity is constrained.

Mission:
Move critical relief commodities from the three depots to the five receiving units over three operational days to meet life-sustaining demand at minimum total cost, balancing transport, vehicle deployment, shortage penalties, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Commodities and Demand: Daily, unit-specific requirements for water, food, and medical supplies must be met. Shortfalls are allowed only where unavoidable and will incur shortage penalties to reflect unmet humanitarian need.
- Stock Position: Outflows from each depot by commodity and day cannot exceed available stocks. Depot resupply beyond the period is not assumed.
- Routing and Risk: Dispatch occurs over discrete depot-to-unit corridors. Activating a route (sending any vehicles on a given depot-to-unit corridor on a given day) triggers a fixed Risk Cost that represents escort teams, route clearance, and overwatch—this cost is incurred regardless of whether one vehicle or multiple vehicles are sent. This fixed security overhead applies per route-day and must be explicitly traded against consolidation of flows.
- Transport and Vehicles: Per-unit transport costs vary by corridor and day due to distance and road condition. Each vehicle has a fixed deployment cost and a volumetric capacity; mixed loads are permitted subject to commodity volume footprints. The total fleet available per day is limited, and the sum of vehicles dispatched across all corridors cannot exceed that limit. Vehicles can only operate on routes that are activated; non-activated corridors cannot carry traffic.
- Prioritization and Consolidation: Given limited fleet and high fixed risk costs, planners will consolidate shipments onto the minimum number of safe corridors that still meet critical needs, prioritizing supplies with the highest shortage penalties (e.g., water and medical) to the most vulnerable units. Where routes are hazardous or throughput is low, consider pooling demand at intermediate units if feasible within the corridor structure.
- Timing and Control: Convoys move in daylight under Movement Control Team oversight. Security Task Force and Engineers allocate clearance and escort assets to the corridors selected for activation. Adjust daily based on changing clearance status and depot drawdown.
